why: True for drags and wheel, but a two-finger pinch writes radius directly, so a scene-less attachControl does move the camera (radius 10 to 5).

Clamping in setters needs setCameraLimits, but interpolateArcRotateCamera reads the limit fields directly, so a lowerRadiusLimit of 5 set by hand stops an interpolation at 5 without setCameraLimits; a same-value write is also not clamped.
Near maps to 1 and far to 0 for perspective, and I also saw the same under enableOrthographicCamera.
The probe reads fov 0.8, nearPlane 0.1 and farPlane 1000 on a new camera, and the factory sets only these.

Holds after the matrix was read once, but a target assigned before the first read is seen at once, and edits to the replacing object are picked up at the next alpha/beta/radius change, so 'never tracked' misleads.
Holds with default limits, but pitch is clamped at the requested radius before radius is clamped: with radiusMax 2R, asking radius 10R and pitch 1 gives radius 2R but pitch 0.001.
Holds for writes between frames, but a pose write made after the call and before its first frame is not detected and the promise resolves.
A second fly calls the first one's finish, which resolves it where it stands; the probe and code agree.
The controls rebuild target from _yaw/_pitch (seeded at creation) on any move or turn, overwriting a later target write.
The probe shows the exact offset formula, the zoom-out sign and the doubling with radius.
Without the installed factory no key listener is added; with it, keydown is on the canvas and tabIndex becomes 0 when no tabindex attribute exists.
The probe shows 0.01 at radius 10 and 0.1 at radius 100 for 50 px with panningInertia 0, and the code scales by radius/1000 at every beta.
Pans decay by panningInertia, not inertia, so with inertia 0 a right-drag pan keeps moving the target on later frames (and radius subtracts its offset).
Beta is clamped only in the rotation branch, alpha is never wrapped, and radius is floored at 0.01 after zoom, as the probe shows.
The probe reads fov 0.8, nearPlane 1, farPlane 10000 on a new free camera.
The probe shows the default pose and that at centre (R,0,0) a tilt at yaw 0 looks along +Z and at yaw PI/2 has no Z part.
The probe shows radiusMin 10, radiusMax 4R, nearPlane 1, farPlane 16R and the radius clamps.

An in-place edit moves nothing at once, but the next yaw, pitch or radius write re-orbits around the edited centre (centre y=R, radius 2R puts position y at 3R), so assigning is not the only way it takes effect.
Button 0 pans, any other button rotates, keys are on window, and tabIndex is not touched.
The cached ortho matrix does persist, but the matrix rebuilt after a fov write keeps the ortho p[15]=1 (and p[12], p[13]), so it is not a clean perspective matrix.
The defaults, the aspect-derived width, the ignored fov and the live halfHeight setter all show in the probe.
The probe shows W climbing on a pitched camera, ArrowUp moving, Space moving only along Y, and a middle drag changing _yaw.
disposeScene clears scene state but leaves the canvas listeners; the returned function removes them all.
The getters return the same cache object, rewritten in place on change or other aspect.
The probe shows the bottom-up to top-down conversion, the clamp to the target, and the aspect scaled by viewport.width/height.
Button 1 maps to no action, a touch with button 0 always rotates, and a mouse primary follows the mapping.
touchmove writes radius = startRadius*startDist/dist directly with no offset and no frame.
True for one held arrow, but two held arrows are normalized, so ArrowRight with ArrowDown adds 0.01/sqrt(2) to alpha, not 0.01.
Alpha takes the short way, ends at the raw goal 2PI+0.1, and a radius goal past upperRadiusLimit ends at the limit.
The zeroing holds, but a disposer only removes its own hook: after a second setCameraLimits call the first disposer leaves the clamping on.
Only keys present are written, and an explicit undefined clears that bound.
Wheel feeds -sign(deltaY), zoom inertia is 0.9 and rotation inertia 0, as the probe shows.
A wheel event with deltaY 0 (a horizontal scroll) adds no zoom and does not end the fly.
Seen only with inertia 0: at the default inertia 0.9 a 100 px downward drag lowers _pitch by about 0.5, ten times pixels/angularSensitivity.
Holds for deltaMs of 1 and above, but deltaMs is floored at 1, so a 0 ms frame still moves speed/sqrt(100000).
fastMultiplier defaults to 1, and upKeys replaces the default list, as the probe shows.
Writing upVector rolls the banked camera at once; a plain free camera has no upVector and uses world +Y.
Each enable builds fresh bounds from the given options, defaulting to halfHeight 1 and null planes.
validateOptions throws RangeError for both cases; projectPointToViewportToRef does no validation.
x and y are not clamped, and a point strictly behind the eye is behindCamera and offscreen with finite coordinates (a point in the eye plane gives NaN).
normalizeRadians wraps to [-PI, PI), giving 4-2PI and -PI.
clampCenterFromPoles keeps the magnitude and caps sin(latitude) at 0.998749218.
dblclick needs button 0 and buttons 0 and a globe hit, then flies over the default 1000 ms.
